A1.justification: Both complete 36-page PDFs present the same work, including Appendices A–G. Their text, equations, algorithms and proofs support reliable comparison despite changes in pagination.

before.justification: v2 reports algorithms, mathematical examples, theoretical bounds and proofs throughout the main text and appendices, without original experimental, simulation, user-study or data-analysis outcomes.

after.justification: v3 reports theoretical algorithms, bounds and proofs in the main text and Appendices A–G. No original empirical outcomes are reported.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1 and 2, ℓ-UCB and ℓ-GOLF, retain identical procedures, losses and confidence-set constructions. Appendix A’s convex relaxation is also unchanged.

E1.justification: Neither version uses datasets or empirically evaluated task scenarios. Both study the same bounded-cost bandit and finite-horizon reinforcement learning settings theoretically.

E2.justification: Neither version experimentally evaluates baselines. The theoretical comparisons with earlier methods, including Faury et al. (2022) and Wang et al. (2023, 2024), are unchanged.

E3.justification: Neither PDF reports empirical evaluation protocols. No data splits, evaluation metrics, experimental budgets, sample sizes or testing procedures are added or revised.

E4.justification: Neither version contains empirical ablations, robustness tests or case studies. The mathematical examples and supplementary arguments are retained unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports empirical run counts, seeds, error bars or significance tests. The theoretical probability guarantees and Bernstein concentration analysis are unchanged.

E6.justification: The regret bounds, eluder-dimension bounds and illustrative findings, including Remark 5 on Bernoullisation, match. Neither version contains empirical performance results.

T1.justification: Definition 2, the assumptions, formal results and proofs in Appendices A–G are unchanged. Although v3 adds a notice describing a corrected definition and corresponding proofs relative to the originally published manuscript, the matching mathematical content already appears in v2.

C1.justification: The abstract, four introductory contributions and Section 6 retain the same claims about localisation, global eluder-dimension lower bounds and first-order regret guarantees for bandits and reinforcement learning.

C2.justification: Section 4.3 retains the same qualifications concerning small-cost versus variance-dependent bounds, analysis-only localisation and Bernoullisation. The reinforcement learning assumptions and applicability discussion are also unchanged.

D1.justification: Algorithm specifications, confidence-width formulas and Appendix A’s convex relaxation are unchanged. No implementation, hardware, computational-resource or code/data-access information is added.

R1.justification: Section 1.1, the subsequent comparisons with prior research and the bibliography contain the same works and positioning. References move across page boundaries without substantive edits.

P1.justification: v3 adds a first-page correction notice and updates the arXiv version/date stamp. The remaining prose, terminology and section organization are unchanged after matching relocated text.

P2.justification: The new first-page notice splits the contribution list across pages 1–2 and causes subsequent text, equations, acknowledgements and references to reflow. Algorithm displays retain their structure, and all appendix pages are visually identical.

improvement.justification: v3 explicitly states its corrected status and the stated scope of the correction on the first page, whereas v2 only acknowledges an earlier serious error near the references. This modestly improves transparency. The definitions, proofs and conclusions already match v2, so the benefit is editorial, with only minor accompanying pagination changes.
